subject: social_science

concepts.title: The Idea and Early Experiments of Satyagraha
concepts.definition: A philosophy of passive mass agitation based on moral force and peaceful appeal to conscience, arguing that injustice can be overcome without vengeance or physical aggression.
concepts.key_idea: Truth and non-violence serve as ethical instruments for collective mobilization against political tyranny.
question_patterns: Explain the core philosophy behind the concept of satyagraha
Describe the three local satyagraha movements organized by Mahatma Gandhi between 1917 and 1918
How did Gandhi differentiate soul-force from passive physical resistance?
Why did the peasants of Kheda organize a satyagraha in 1918?
What role did the Champaran movement play in the evolution of Indian nationalism?

solution_steps.explain: State that satyagraha relies on truth and non-violence rather than weaponized force to persuade the oppressor's conscience.
List the Champaran agitation (1917) against indigo plantations, the Kheda movement (1918) for revenue relaxation, and the Ahmedabad mill workers strike (1918).
Explain how these early successes established mass contact and tested Gandhian methods on Indian soil.

concepts.title: The Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh Massacre
concepts.definition: A repressive colonial enactment permitting preventive detention of political dissidents without trial, which provoked nationwide strikes and culminated in the Amritsar massacre.
concepts.key_idea: State repression of peaceful demonstrations galvanized popular outrage into widespread anti-colonial resistance.
question_patterns: Why did Indians vehemently oppose the Rowlatt Act of 1919?
Describe the events leading to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre on 13 April 1919
What was General Dyer's stated objective behind the firing at Jallianwala Bagh?
Explain the methods used by the colonial regime to suppress the Rowlatt satyagraha
How did the country react to the news of the Amritsar massacre?

solution_steps.explain: Explain that the Rowlatt Act empowered the imperial government to detain political suspects for up to two years without judicial trial.
Outline the nationwide hartal of 6 April, the arrest of local leaders in Amritsar, and the declaration of martial law.
Narrate the unprovoked firing on the Baisakhi gathering in Jallianwala Bagh, resulting in widespread riots, brutal state floggings, and the movement's suspension.

concepts.title: The Khilafat Issue and the Launch of Non-Cooperation
concepts.definition: A joint anti-imperial platform uniting Indian Muslims defending the Ottoman Caliph's temporal authority with the broader nationalist struggle for self-governance.
concepts.key_idea: Nationalist leadership leveraged shared anti-colonial grievances to forge Hindu-Muslim unity and initiate staged non-cooperation.
question_patterns: Why did Mahatma Gandhi decide to take up the Khilafat issue?
What rationale did Gandhi offer in Hind Swaraj for withdrawing cooperation from the British?
Outline the staged programme of the Non-Cooperation Movement adopted at the Nagpur Congress session
Who founded the Khilafat Committee in Bombay and why?
Discuss the initial reluctance within the Congress regarding the boycott of legislative councils in 1920

solution_steps.explain: Explain that the post-WWI treatment of Ottoman Turkey created Muslim anger, leading the Ali brothers to form the Khilafat Committee.
Note Gandhi's argument in Hind Swaraj that colonial rule survived solely due to Indian collaboration.
Outline the progressive surrender of state titles, boycott of civil posts, schools, law courts, foreign textiles, and eventual council election boycotts ratified at Nagpur in December 1920.

concepts.title: Non-Cooperation Movement in Towns and Economic Effects
concepts.definition: Urban manifestation of the national agitation where educated middle classes boycotted colonial institutions, legal courts, and foreign commodities, fostering domestic production.
concepts.key_idea: While initial urban boycott caused economic disruption to British imports, the lack of indigenous infrastructure slowed middle-class participation.
question_patterns: How did the middle-class population in cities participate in the Non-Cooperation Movement?
What were the economic effects of the boycott of foreign cloth between 1921 and 1922?
Why did the Non-Cooperation Movement in urban centres gradually lose momentum?
Why did the Justice Party in Madras decide not to boycott council elections?
Examine the challenges faced by poor town dwellers in sustaining the boycott of mill-made cloth

solution_steps.explain: State that students left government schools, teachers resigned, lawyers left courts, and council elections were boycotted in most provinces.
Explain that foreign cloth imports halved in value from 102 crore to 57 crore rupees, liquor shops were picketed, and domestic handloom production expanded.
Highlight the prohibitive cost of khadi over machine fabric and the scarcity of alternative national schools and courts to absorb returning participants.

concepts.title: Peasant and Tribal Movements in the Countryside
concepts.definition: Rural and forest-based insurgencies against oppressive landlords and colonial forest acts, frequently blending local aspirations with messianic invocations of Swaraj.
concepts.key_idea: Subaltern agrarian and tribal communities reinterpreted the nationalist message through the prism of their immediate socio-economic oppressions.
question_patterns: Explain the peasant movement led by Baba Ramchandra in Awadh during 1920-21
What were the primary grievances of tribal peasants in the Gudem Hills of Andhra Pradesh?
Describe the leadership and methods adopted by Alluri Sitaram Raju in the forest rebellion
How did the peasant demands in Awadh differ from the official Congress programme?
What led to the establishment of the Oudh Kisan Sabha in 1920?

solution_steps.explain: Describe Baba Ramchandra's leadership against extortionate rents, begar (unpaid labor), tenure insecurity, and the formation of Oudh Kisan Sabha.
Explain how British forest enclosures restricted grazing and firewood collection, sparking Alluri Sitaram Raju's armed guerrilla campaign.

solution_steps.action: contrast local actions with mainstream non-violence
solution_steps.explain: Highlight peasant attacks on talukdar manors, grain looting, and violent clashes that deviated from Gandhian non-violent discipline.

concepts.title: Swaraj in the Plantations and the Chauri Chaura Incident
concepts.definition: The defiance of coercive labor containment laws by plantation workers seeking freedom of mobility, followed by the abrupt withdrawal of Non-Cooperation due to police-crowd violence.
concepts.key_idea: Workers conceived freedom as spatial mobility and village restoration, while escalating local violence forced the suspension of the nationwide struggle.
question_patterns: How did plantation workers in Assam interpret the concept of Swaraj?
What restrictions were imposed on tea estate laborers under the Inland Emigration Act of 1859?
Explain why Mahatma Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922
Describe the tragedy faced by plantation laborers stranded during their journey home
What was the significance of the Chauri Chaura incident in Gorakhpur?

solution_steps.action: state legal constraint on tea workers
solution_steps.explain: Identify the Inland Emigration Act of 1859 which barred tea workers from leaving plantations without rarely granted permits.
Explain that thousands left estates hoping for land distribution in Gandhi Raj, but were stranded and beaten during railway strikes.
Detail the February 1922 violent clash at Chauri Chaura where a mob set a police post on fire, prompting Gandhi to call off Non-Cooperation.

concepts.title: The Simon Commission and the Demand for Purna Swaraj
concepts.definition: The political escalation sparked by an all-British statutory constitutional commission, culminating in the Indian National Congress adopting total independence as its goal.
concepts.key_idea: Exclusion of Indian representatives from constitutional inquiries unified diverse political factions toward demanding complete sovereignty.
question_patterns: Why was the Simon Commission boycotted by all major political parties in India?
What was the significance of the Lahore Congress session of December 1929?
How did the Great Depression impact agrarian conditions in India during the late 1920s?
Explain the role of the Swaraj Party formed by C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru
What was declared in the Independence Day pledge of 26 January 1930?

solution_steps.explain: Explain that the 1928 Statutory Commission under Sir John Simon had no Indian members, triggering demonstrations under 'Go Back Simon'.

solution_steps.action: assess economic and internal political factors
solution_steps.explain: Note the collapse of farm prices after 1926-1930 and the debate between Swarajist council-entry advocates and radical youths like Nehru and Bose.
State that the Lahore Congress under Jawaharlal Nehru adopted 'Purna Swaraj' (complete independence) and designated 26 January 1930 as Independence Day.

concepts.title: The Salt March and the Civil Disobedience Movement
concepts.section: 3.1 The Salt March and the Civil Disobedience Movement
concepts.definition: A symbolic nationwide campaign begun by breaking the British salt monopoly, transitioning the national struggle from non-cooperation to active lawbreaking.
concepts.key_idea: Choosing a universal daily commodity like salt enabled Gandhi to unite disparate socio-economic strata against colonial fiscal tyranny.
question_patterns: Why did Mahatma Gandhi choose salt as the central symbol for his campaign in 1930?
Describe the course of the Dandi March from Sabarmati to the Gujarat coast
How did Civil Disobedience fundamentally differ from the Non-Cooperation Movement?
What were the terms and outcomes of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed in March 1931?
How did the colonial government react to the launch of the Civil Disobedience Movement?

solution_steps.explain: Show that the government monopoly and taxation on salt burdened every social class, making it an ideal unifying issue.
Trace the 240-mile march of 78 volunteers over 24 days ending with the ceremonial boiling of seawater on 6 April 1930.

solution_steps.action: outline mass actions and state response
solution_steps.explain: Detail widespread breaking of salt laws, forest law defiance, refusal of chaukidari taxes, mass arrests of nearly 100,000 satyagrahis, and the temporary truce of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

concepts.title: Social Participation in Civil Disobedience: Rural and Business Strata
concepts.definition: The diverse socio-economic alignment of rich farmers, tenant peasants, Indian merchants, mine workers, and women within the Civil Disobedience campaign.
concepts.key_idea: Different socio-economic classes joined the struggle with divergent class interests, which created strategic compromises within the national leadership.
question_patterns: Why did rich peasant communities like Patidars and Jats participate enthusiastically in 1930 but refuse in 1932?
Why was the Indian National Congress reluctant to support the 'no-rent' campaigns of poor tenants?
Explain the role of business leaders and industrial organizations like FICCI in the Civil Disobedience Movement
Describe the nature and extent of women's participation during the Salt Satyagraha
Why was working-class participation limited during the Civil Disobedience Movement?

solution_steps.explain: Differentiate rich commercial crop producers demanding revenue reduction from poor tenant farmers demanding rent remission.
Detail the role of business bodies (FICCI, Indian Industrial and Commercial Congress) and industrialists (G.D. Birla, Purshottamdas Thakurdas) demanding trade protection.

solution_steps.action: evaluate participation of women and workers
solution_steps.explain: Highlight large-scale urban middle-class and rural wealthy women picketing shops, alongside selective labor strikes in railways and Chotanagpur mines.

concepts.title: Limits of Civil Disobedience: Dalit Representation and Poona Pact
concepts.definition: The social and political divides around separate electorates for marginalized communities that culminated in an agreement preserving joint electorates with reserved seats.
concepts.key_idea: Socio-political empowerment of depressed classes and minority representation highlighted internal structural contradictions within the anti-colonial front.
question_patterns: Why was Dalit participation restricted during the Civil Disobedience Movement?
What was the main point of conflict between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar at the Second Round Table Conference?
Explain the key provisions and significance of the Poona Pact of September 1932
Why did Muslim political organizations show a lukewarm response to Civil Disobedience?
How did negotiations on legislative seat reservation break down between the Congress and the Muslim League?

solution_steps.explain: Explain Dr. Ambedkar's demand through the Depressed Classes Association for separate electorates to secure political leverage for Dalits.
Describe Gandhi's fast unto death based on the conviction that separate electorates would permanently fracture Hindu society.
State the terms of the September 1932 pact granting reserved seats in provincial and central councils for Depressed Classes within a joint general electorate.

concepts.title: Cultural Expressions and the Sense of Collective Belonging
concepts.definition: The creation of a unified national identity through allegorical visual representations, patriotic songs, folklore preservation, flag symbolism, and historical reinterpretation.
concepts.key_idea: Cultural artifacts and historical memory mobilized popular emotion to imagine a shared Indian identity across diverse regional and linguistic lines.
question_patterns: How did the visual image of Bharat Mata help create a sense of national identity?
Explain the role of folklore and songs in the revival of national pride during the independence movement
Describe the evolution of the Indian national flag from the Swadeshi tricolour to the Swaraj flag of 1921
How did the reinterpretation of ancient Indian history instill national pride?
What challenges arose when nationalist imagery relied heavily on ancient Hindu symbols?

solution_steps.explain: Detail Bankim Chandra's 'Vande Mataram' and Abanindranath Tagore's ascetic portrayal of Bharat Mata dispensing food, cloth, and wisdom.
Describe Natesa Sastri's Tamil folk collections, Rabindranath Tagore's ballads, the 1905 eight-lotus Swadeshi flag, and Gandhi's 1921 charkha Swaraj flag.
Show how rediscovering ancient artistic and scientific achievements generated pride, but sometimes alienated non-Hindu minorities when past symbols were exclusively Hindu.

concepts.title: The Quit India Movement of 1942
concepts.definition: A decisive, widespread mass uprising launched during World War II demanding immediate unconditional termination of British colonial governance in India.
concepts.key_idea: The total mobilization under the call 'Do or Die' incapacitated colonial administrative machinery across vast territories.
question_patterns: What circumstances led to the launch of the Quit India Movement in August 1942?
Explain the significance of Mahatma Gandhi's 'Do or Die' mantra during Quit India
Name prominent leaders and women participants who spearheaded underground resistance during Quit India
How did ordinary citizens participate in the Quit India struggle across various provinces?
Describe the extent of administrative paralysis caused by the Quit India Movement

solution_steps.explain: State that the collapse of the Cripps Mission and wartime price crises prompted the Congress Working Committee resolution at Wardha and AICC approval at Bombay in August 1942.
Identify Gandhi's 'Do or Die' exhortation and the role of underground leaders such as Jayprakash Narayan, Aruna Asaf Ali, Ram Manohar Lohia, Matangini Hazra, and Kanaklata Barua.

solution_steps.action: summarize mass action and colonial suppression
solution_steps.explain: Explain how strikes, attacks on communication links, and widespread peasant actions paralyzed government apparatus until crushed by force over a year.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Explain how the First World War created new economic and political conditions that aided the growth of the national movement in India.

solution_template.explain: The war led to enormous increases in colonial defence expenditure, financed through war loans, heightened customs duties, and the introduction of income tax.
Extreme price inflation caused commodity prices to double between 1913 and 1918, while forced rural recruitment for the imperial army created deep resentment.

solution_template.action: link famines and epidemics to political discontent
solution_template.explain: Widespread crop failures in 1918-19 and 1920-21 alongside the influenza epidemic resulted in 12 to 13 million deaths, uniting people against colonial neglect.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Analyze the reasons behind the signing of the Poona Pact between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar in 1932.

solution_template.explain: Dr. Ambedkar demanded separate electorates for the Depressed Classes at the Second Round Table Conference, which the British government granted.
Gandhi undertook a fast unto death in Yerwada jail, arguing that separate electorates would permanently segregate Dalits and impede their social integration.
The Poona Pact of September 1932 conceded reserved seats for the Depressed Classes in provincial and central legislatures while retaining joint voting by the general electorate.

questions: Explain why the growth of modern nationalism in colonies like India is intimately connected to anti-colonial movements.
How did the First World War help in creating a favorable ground for the growth of the national movement in India?
Why were Indians from various walks of life outraged by the hurried passage of the Rowlatt Act in 1919?
Why did Mahatma Gandhi decide to abruptly withdraw the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922?
What did Mahatma Gandhi mean by the idea of satyagraha as an active, soul-force rather than passive resistance?
Write a detailed newspaper report on the Jallianwala Bagh massacre describing the events of 13 April 1919.
Write a report on the arrival and nationwide boycott of the Simon Commission in 1928.
Compare the visual representation and attributes of Bharat Mata with the allegorical image of Germania.
List the various social groups that participated in the Non-Cooperation Movement of 1921 and analyze the aspirations of any three.
Discuss the Salt March to demonstrate why salt served as an exceptionally effective symbol of resistance against colonial rule.
Imagine you are an urban middle-class woman participating in the Civil Disobedience Movement of 1930; explain your motivations and experiences.
Why did political leaders differ sharply over the question of separate electorates for minority and depressed communities?
